entries.title: Public Secrets
entries.author: Nora Roberts
entries.text: Emma McAvoy grows up in the spotlight, but the privileged world around her cannot protect her family from tragedy. Years later, as she builds a career and considers marriage, an unresolved crime brings childhood memories back into focus. A homicide detective's determination to uncover the truth makes those fragments increasingly important. Nora Roberts combines family history, romantic suspense and the pressures of public life in a story about a past that someone is still prepared to kill to conceal.

entries.title: Private Scandals
entries.author: Nora Roberts
entries.text: Deanna Reynolds has ambitions beyond her position in a Chicago television newsroom. When her mentor, Angela Perkins, moves to New York, Deanna gets an opportunity to develop the career and programme she wants. Her success also draws the attention of reporter Finn Riley. Angela, however, sees her former colleague's rise very differently. This romantic suspense novel follows the rivalry behind television's polished public image, where professional ambition, personal betrayal and a determination to retaliate become dangerously entangled.

entries.title: Sonnets
entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.text: Shakespeare's sequence of 154 sonnets explores love through admiration, jealousy, disappointment and the awareness that beauty cannot last. A young man, a woman and a rival poet figure in the speaker's shifting concerns, while time and mortality repeatedly threaten what the poems celebrate. The collection also asks whether verse can preserve a person beyond ordinary life. Its changing voices and relationships invite interpretation without establishing that the people or events described are a straightforward account of Shakespeare's own biography.

entries.title: Richard III
entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.text: Richard, Duke of Gloucester, sets his sights on the English crown while his brother Edward IV still rules. He works through persuasion, calculated accusations and violence, turning family relationships into instruments of political advancement. His courtship of Lady Anne and his treatment of rival claimants reveal how readily he changes his public role to suit an opportunity. Shakespeare's history play follows the struggle for power within a royal family, examining manipulation, loyalty and the human consequences of Richard's ambition.

entries.title: Fantastic Mr. Fox (Windrush)
entries.author: Roald Dahl
entries.text: Three farmers, Boggis, Bunce and Bean, are determined to put an end to Mr Fox's raids. Their attempts to catch him escalate into a campaign to shoot him, dig him out or starve him underground. Mr Fox must rely on ingenuity as the farmers close in on his home. Roald Dahl turns this contest between a resourceful animal and his relentless pursuers into a comic adventure, with an escape plan that depends on thinking beyond the trap the farmers have set.

entries.title: James and the Giant Peach
entries.author: Roald Dahl
entries.text: After losing his parents, James Henry Trotter lives with two cruel aunts, Spiker and Sponge. His unhappy life changes when a strange gift leads to an extraordinary peach growing in their garden. Inside, James encounters enormous insects who become companions on an adventure far beyond the home he wants to leave. Roald Dahl's story moves from an oppressive household into a fantastical journey, giving an isolated child the chance to find friendship, take risks and discover a different kind of family.

entries.title: Romeo and Juliet
entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.text: The Montagues and Capulets are enemies, but Romeo and Juliet fall in love when they meet at a gathering in the Capulet household. They seek a future together in secret, with Friar Lawrence helping them marry despite the feud. Violence in Verona soon makes that hope harder to protect. Shakespeare's tragedy places youthful desire beside family loyalty, public conflict and hurried decisions, showing how the lovers' private plans are constrained by the hostility of the world around them.

entries.title: Henry V
entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.text: Having become king of England, Henry lays claim to the French throne and takes his army across the Channel. The campaign brings sieges, negotiations and the prospect of battle at Agincourt, while Henry must persuade others to accept his authority and share the risks of war. Shakespeare's history play considers leadership through both royal speeches and the experiences of soldiers. Its portrait of conquest brings questions of legitimacy, responsibility and the cost of military ambition into the same story.

entries.title: Maximum Security (CHERUB)
entries.author: Robert Muchamore
entries.text: James's third CHERUB mission takes him inside Arizona Max, a prison holding young offenders. His assignment is to get close to an arms dealer's son, whose father is supplying missiles to terrorists. Reaching the father requires more than gaining the boy's confidence: James must help engineer an escape. The operation puts a trained teenage agent in a place where his cover offers little protection from daily danger, and where the route to a much larger target runs through another prisoner's trust.

entries.title: Wishtree
entries.author: Katherine Applegate
entries.text: Red is an old oak tree whose branches hold the wishes that neighbours write on pieces of cloth. With Bongo the crow and the animals sheltering in the tree's hollows, Red has watched generations of people come and go. A newly arrived family encounters a welcome that is far from universal, giving the neighbourhood's familiar tradition new significance. Katherine Applegate tells this children's novel from the tree's perspective, connecting a community's treatment of newcomers with friendship, shelter and the hopes people share.

entries.author: Rina Kent
entries.text: Cecily Knight enters the Heathens' initiation competition to gather information for a rival group, expecting to remain unnoticed. Instead, she attracts Jeremy Volkov, the Heathens' leader and heir to a Russian criminal family. His pursuit draws her toward a world she intended only to observe, while his claims of protection conceal a desire for control. The third Legacy of Gods novel is a dark college romance built around opposing loyalties, criminal power and Cecily's resistance to Jeremy's possessiveness.

entries.title: Endless Night
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: Michael Rogers imagines a different life when he sees Gipsy's Acre, a site where he could build a beautiful house overlooking the sea and settle with the woman he loves. The possibility of that future comes with warnings about the place, followed by disturbing events that undermine its promise. Agatha Christie's suspense novel centres on the gap between an apparently fortunate new beginning and the fears gathering around it, asking how much of the danger belongs to superstition and how much to people.

entries.text: Princess Winter is admired by the people of Luna, despite the scars on her face and the contempt of her stepmother, Queen Levana. As Cinder and her allies prepare to challenge Levana, Winter has a part to play in the struggle. The fourth Lunar Chronicles novel brings the series' central characters into a confrontation over tyranny, loyalty and the future of both Luna and Earth.

entries.title: Five Little Pigs
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: Caroline Crale was convicted of poisoning her husband sixteen years ago. When Hercule Poirot revisits the case, he must work with memories rather than a fresh crime scene, examining the accounts of five people connected to the death. Each remembers events through a different set of loyalties, assumptions and grievances. Agatha Christie's mystery makes the distance between observation and interpretation central to the investigation, as Poirot tests whether the accepted explanation can survive a careful comparison of those competing recollections.

entries.title: Evil Under the Sun
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: Hercule Poirot's seaside holiday is interrupted when Arlena Stuart is found strangled on a beach. Her presence at the resort has already stirred jealousy and attraction, making a crime of passion seem an obvious explanation. Poirot examines the guests' movements and relationships to discover whether that appearance is reliable. Set within a holiday community where people watch one another closely but understand less than they think, this mystery turns leisure, gossip and apparently ordinary encounters into possible evidence.

entries.title: Bittersweet Passion
entries.author: Lynne Graham
entries.text: Claire Fletcher's grandfather makes her inheritance conditional on marrying one of his grandsons. She turns to Dane Visconti, the family outsider she has long trusted and admired, hoping he will agree to a practical arrangement. Claire promises not to expect more than the marriage requires, but Dane has conditions of his own. Lynne Graham's romance begins with a financial bargain and explores how unequal expectations, family pressures and an existing emotional attachment complicate a supposedly convenient solution.

entries.title: The Other Woman
entries.author: Jessica Steele
entries.text: Georgina's new boss, Tallis York, believes she has been involved with Desmond Warner, her cousin's estranged husband. The accusation places her in an uncomfortable position at work, especially when she cannot easily dispel the gossip surrounding the relationship. Tallis's opinion begins to matter to her for reasons beyond her employment. Jessica Steele's romance follows the tension between an assumed betrayal and Georgina's actual circumstances, as misunderstanding interferes with the possibility of a different relationship between employee and employer.

Robb, this third In Death novel places a personally difficult murder inquiry in a future New York whose technological possibilities offer little protection from jealousy and greed.

entries.title: Towards Zero
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: An unsuccessful suicide attempt, a schoolgirl's wrongful accusation of theft and a tennis player's troubled relationships seem to belong to separate stories. Their significance changes as events converge at Gull's Point, where a house party ends in the murder of an elderly widow. Agatha Christie builds this mystery around the circumstances that lead people toward a crime. The investigation must look beyond the immediate scene to understand how apparently disconnected experiences have helped create the moment when the killing becomes possible.

entries.title: The Arabian Mistress
entries.author: Lynne Graham
entries.text: Faye has not seen Prince Tariq since their wedding a year earlier. When her brother is imprisoned in Tariq's homeland, she must appeal to the husband from whom she has been separated. Tariq offers help on a condition that turns their existing marriage into a new struggle: he wants her to return as his mistress. Lynne Graham's romance centres on an estranged couple whose reunion is driven by family pressure, resentment and an imbalance of power that complicates their renewed attraction.

The second Empire novel develops a dark workplace romance around concealment, recognition and a powerful employer determined to pursue their unfinished connection.

entries.text: Darcy agrees to deliver a letter without knowing that it is part of a blackmail attempt. Neve Macalister assumes she is involved and abducts her, turning an apparently simple errand into a frightening confrontation. Jessica Steele's romance begins with a serious misjudgment and follows the uneasy relationship left behind when suspicion gives way to a different understanding.

entries.text: Clare Harper's time in Greece is disrupted by Lazar Vardakas, who accuses her brother of seducing his sister. Clare rejects his account, but Lazar's determination to retaliate makes her the target of a dispute she did not create. Their confrontation becomes entangled with attraction, without removing the pressure of the original accusation. Jessica Steele's romance explores how family allegiance and assumptions about another person's conduct can drive an increasingly personal conflict between two people who distrust each other's motives.

Lynne Graham's romance connects their developing relationship with a struggle over family obligations, royal authority and who gets to decide the child's future.

The ninth book combines an urgent inquiry into the crash with the challenges of undercover work among young people.

The first Throne Duet novel follows a dark romance shaped by criminal hierarchy, competing plans and a struggle over which partner will control the future they are supposed to share.

entries.title: Voetnoot
entries.author: Arnon Grunberg
entries.text: Deze eerste verzameling bundelt korte columns die Arnon Grunberg voor de voorpagina van de Volkskrant schreef. In zijn voetnoten bij de actualiteit bekijkt hij publieke gebeurtenissen, alledaagse opvattingen en menselijke tegenstrijdigheden vanuit onverwachte hoeken. Bob Polak stelde de selectie samen. Het boek bevat daarnaast een vraaggesprek waarin Polak eenendertig vragen stelt en Grunberg negenentwintig antwoorden geeft. De beknopte stukken laten zien hoe Grunberg met weinig woorden een standpunt kan onderzoeken, een vanzelfsprekendheid ter discussie stelt of de absurditeit van een situatie blootlegt.
